deviations: Pooled US-UK regressions (Table 1 cols 3-4) use a baseline year spline common to all observations plus the spline interacted with a US indicator (and a US indicator), so the US interaction coefficients are US-minus-UK slopes. The paper describes the baseline as a spline 'for the comparison country'; read literally as a UK-only spline, the US terms would just reproduce the US-only slopes, which contradicts the paper's description of them as relative to the UK.

Engine sample is all United States rows of engine_data.dta with non-missing ln_hp_per_lbs (85). The file has no aircraft-type variable, so I assumed it already holds only engines used in fighters and bombers (every US row has a non-missing count from the airframe match).
notes: Airframe sample: airframe_data.dta, type fighter or bomber, years 1918-1935, US (cols 1-2) or US+UK (cols 3-4), non-missing outcome. Continuous two-piece spline with each coefficient equal to its segment's slope: pre = min(year,1926)-1926, post = max(year,1926)-1926. OLS with heteroskedasticity-robust SEs (fixest). Engine regression adds a liquid-cooled indicator. attempt-1 was exploratory (data inspection, no RESULT lines). attempt-2 was the first scored run; its pooled spec used separate US and UK splines, so its 'vs UK' coefficients were the US-only slopes rather than relative slopes. I fixed that from the paper's text (no claimed values were seen or compared), and the result is the final run. No Docker hangs.
